flawed_step: The claim wrongly assumes that stable 2-WL colours determine every finite graph up to isomorphism.
counterexample: Take the 4×4 rook graph R and the Shrikhande graph S. Both have vertex set Z_4×Z_4. In R, distinct (i,j),(i',j') are adjacent iff i=i' or j=j'. In S, x and y are adjacent iff y−x is in {±(1,0),±(0,1),±(1,1)}. Both are strongly regular with parameters (16,6,2,2): every vertex has 6 neighbors, and every two distinct vertices have exactly 2 common neighbors. Consequently, throughout folklore 2-WL, pair colours depend only on whether a pair is diagonal, adjacent, or nonadjacent, with identical refinement data in both graphs. Their stable ordered-pair colour multiplicities are therefore 16, 96, and 144, so 2-WL does not distinguish them. Yet they are non-isomorphic: R contains a 4-clique (any row), while S contains none. Indeed, the six neighbors of any vertex in S induce a 6-cycle, so no three of them form the triangle required to extend that vertex to a 4-clique.
assessment_summary: The non-isomorphic rook and Shrikhande graphs have the same strongly regular parameters and hence identical stable 2-WL colour multisets.
